title: Lava Lamp: Blobs That Dance
description: Oil, water and one fizzy tablet make blobs that rise, bloom and sink in slow motion. Build a table-top lava lamp and learn why the blobs can't decide where to live.

body.heading: A lamp with no lightbulb
paragraphs: A real lava lamp needs heat and patience. Yours needs neither — just oil, water and fizz. Within seconds of dropping in a tablet piece, coloured blobs begin a slow, endless dance: up, bloom, down, again. It is the most relaxing science model in this whole collection.

body.heading: Meet the parts
paragraphs: The oil — the clear golden ocean that fills most of the bottle; it never mixes with water. The water — coloured, sitting in a layer at the bottom, denser than the oil. The fizz — pieces of an effervescent tablet, which make bubbles of gas when they meet water. The bottle — tall and clear, so the whole dance is visible. A torch underneath is the stage light.

body.heading: You will need
paragraphs: A clear plastic bottle or tall glass, cooking oil, water, food colouring, effervescent tablets (the vitamin or antacid kind — a grown-up keeps and handles them), and a torch or phone light for the stage lighting.

body.heading: How it works — step by step
paragraphs: Step 1 — Pour the water layer. Fill the bottle about a quarter full with water and stir in food colouring until it is deep and jewel-bright.
Step 2 — Add the oil, slowly, down the side. It will slide over the water and settle on top — oil and water never mix, and oil is lighter, so the layers sort themselves.

Step 3 — A grown-up breaks a tablet into quarters and drops ONE piece in. Watch the bottom: fizz! Bubbles form in the water, grab blobs of coloured water, and carry them up through the oil like tiny elevators.

Step 4 — Watch the top. When a blob reaches the surface, its bubbles pop and escape — and the blob, suddenly heavier again, sinks slowly back down to reload. Add another piece whenever the dancing slows.

body.heading: The science bit
paragraphs: Two rules run this show. First: oil and water never mix, and water is denser, so water stays below. Second: the tablet's fizz makes gas bubbles, and a blob of water wearing a coat of bubbles becomes LIGHTER overall than the oil around it — so it floats up. At the top the bubbles pop, the coat is gone, the blob is dense water again, and down it sinks. Rise, pop, sink, repeat — a density elevator that runs until the fizz runs out.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Why does the blob rise only while it is wearing bubbles?
2. What do you think happens if you drop the tablet into a bottle of ONLY oil? Predict, then ask your grown-up if you may test it.

takeaway: Fizz bubbles coat blobs of coloured water and make them lighter than the oil, so they rise; when the bubbles pop at the top, the blobs are dense again and sink.
materials: Clear plastic bottle or tall glass
supervision: A grown-up handles the tablets, adds every piece, and supervises the lamp from start to finish.
safetyNotes: Effervescent tablets are NOT sweets — they may be medicine. A grown-up keeps them in their packet, breaks and drops every piece, and they are never tasted or handled by children.
The lava lamp is a model, never a drink: it contains oil and tablet water. Label the bottle LAVA LAMP and keep it away from cups and younger children.
Shine the torch from under or beside the bottle, never into anyone's eyes, and wipe oil drips at once — oil on floors is a slipping hazard.
screenFreeExtension: Blob meditation minute: set the lamp where the family can see it, start a fresh fizz, and everyone watches in silence for one whole minute — then each person describes the best blob they saw.
